Title: on deals, the Club, and play...

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
My thread! Mine! Mine!

Seriously, there are plenty of other threads running about with variants; I
just want to shovel it all out separately so it doesn't get lost in the
shuffle.

So, on deals. Pat has "outed" me; I did, in fact, do an Evil Thing at
DragonCon and offer a 3-2 (rollover) deal to my predator at about the 1:15
mark of the 3rd round. Though I was already in possession of 1VP (thou
shalt not suffer the Lucian Mind-Rape deck to live), it was certainly
justified as I was looking at a big zero otherwise, with intercept/combat
in front of me and vote/combat behind me. Afraid that my Tzimisce voters
were packing plenty of aggravated eye-poke to counter his Grapple Potence,
he accepted the deal, and it pretty much went down as Pat described in his
own message. Pat eventually transferred himself out to prevent one, I got
my 2nd, then conceded the last 2 with five minutes remaining. Why?
Because the only combat cards in my deck were 6 Meld with the Land, and
while breaking the deal could possibly have resulted in a timeout, it
seemed like a bad idea to risk it - I no longer had vote lock and it would
have become rapidly obvious that I had been snowing him the entire game.

So while that's an example of a suitable rollover (since you can't
profitably break the deal, better keep it), I saw quite a few examples of
unwise rollovers and table-splits throughout DragonCon... especially at the
four-player tables, where a 2-2 isn't inherently "losing". People with
excellent positions were backing off and dumping into 2-2 deals almost out
of habit, it seemed; and that's something I don't like to see. While it
does come with its own penalty (2 VP per round isn't always enough to make
the finals), it very much strikes me as being bad for the game in general.

It's one thing to look at a player cross-table and say "Let's get rid of
the other 2/3 players and fight this out for the last 2"; it's another
thing to automatically go tits-up without testing things, or worse, to sit
and both withdraw (?!) even though there's plenty of time left in the round
to fight it out. This sort of thing is just plain bad for anyone who's
new; they won't be aware of what's happening until it's too late, and then
how do you explain it other than "that's the way it's always been?" Plus,
it really seems to me to be ducking the whole POINT of the game. Millenia-
old enemies do not suddenly "make nice" without plenty of self-interest
involve, and the idea of eventually 'winning.'

I'm not going to keep ranting on that line. And I do agree that it's silly
to try to ban roll-overs and dumping; it's just impossible to prove without
someone sitting there the whole time watching. I believe that the new VP
ideas that are filtering through the pipe are now absolutely MUCH more
necessary than they were before, though. I don't object to the idea of
making deals and splitting tables; what I do object to is the blithe
rollover at the end of it all. Any new rules that reward table wins over
simple VP gain should go a long way in that department; it's still QUITE
possible to dice up a table and remain adversaries after the other 3
players are gone (Mike Ooi and I did it quite tidily in round 2 of the
Dragon's Breath).

With any luck, we'll see the new/proposed VP structure fairly soon.

So, on to the Club. Gosh, everyone just loves this card, don't they? Rob
Treasure (see .sig) had a good point that I had echoed privately for a
couple weeks prior to DragonCon; what happens if the guy you give all your
minions to just keeps them? I know that I personally had PLANNED on
angling for, and then breaking any Club deal that involved someone giving
me all their stuff, partly as a way to pick up a bunch of cheap VP (i'm
greedy), and partly as a way to rattle some sense back into the game (see
above rant). THAT sort of deal also begins shaking the foundations of the
game, IMO; not so much in terms of "why would Methuselahs do this?" as
opposed to just sheer power in the mechanics.

Right now, most tournament decks are usually balanced on a very fine point
(assuming the other 4 decks on the table are comparable in quality). The
reason cross-table deals are so effective is that it doesn't often take a
great deal of pressure to tip a deck's balance out of whack and get it
ousted; sometimes just the extra point of damage from KRC's repeated a few
times is enough, sometimes just a single cross-table Rush removing a key
minion will do. Succubus Club enables the instant creation of an ENORMOUS
imbalance in the game, one that no deck can properly prepare for.

Someone else has already pointed this out, but to all the people saying
"Just put Arsons in! Just put Sudden Reversal in!"... It doesn't work that
way. When you resort to that line of argument, you're creating the old X
and anti-X problem, where you either play with X (the Club), with anti-X
(SR and location-hosers), or you are at a marked disadvantage (you can't
stop the Club from being used against you). Nobody should be FORCED to
play with any given subset of cards. Despite common sightings, it is
possible to make a tournament-quality deck without Deflection or any
"bounce" card (I made it to the final of the Eternal Vigilance tournament
at D*C with one such deck). It is possible to make one without Sudden
Reversal, or Minion Tap, or Blood Doll. It should be possible to make one
without location-hosers.

And, as someone else pointed out, many people's answer to Return to
Innocence was "put Deflections in!", which is exactly the same X/anti-X
situation.

What should be done with the Club? I don't know for sure. I know I don't
like banning cards; and I don't think the Club needs to be BANNED, because
some clever lying and a couple good deal-breaks would really put the fear
of God into routine Club-users. I would hope that the new VP rules would
also affect the Club's usefulness as well... with it being less profitable
to "automatically" make deals, focusing on the Club would be less usable.

However, I also have no faith in people. I think people will try anything
they can to win from their chair, as opposed to on the table; and as long
as people let them get away with it, they'll keep doing it. SC probably
deserves some errata and/or rulings; the most obvious is just to add a
"counter" system to it, much like Palla Grande, Dreams, etc. have now.
Every time the Club is used for a trade, put a counter on it; when the card
has 3 counters, burn the card. This doesn't even remotely wallpaper SC, as
it's a free card anyway; many decks could still make use of it, even given
limited trades. But the back-and-forth trading with the Club (and
wholesale shoveling of cards and minions across the table) would be sharply
limited... is it REALLY profitable to give someone all your minions (1
counter), get them all back (2 counters), and then give them away again (3
counters)?

-- Derek

his neighbors -- to dislodge the worms.

Actually, somewhere, somehow I have to imagine it's been done and in a big
way. For some reason, at the moment most all players seem to be playing their
reputation rather than a couple extra victory points. Maybe most people figure
that a good reputation will get them more chances at the finals in the long run.
So rather than cash in on a sure one right now, they'd rather take their chances

what keeps the double-crosses from balancing out the advantages of making
victory point deals. I only know that it's not happening right now.

Honestly, the whole time I was following these threads, I kept thinking that
this would be a great solution to the problem. Betrayal and Lies. They're
ugly, sure, but ultimately they're tools just as effective as table splits,
intimidation and Jedi Mind Tricks.

However, most people won't do this from what I can tell. I mean, personally,
I value my reputation for honesty and integrity... *outside* the game.

In the game, I suffer no moral quandaries about breaking deals or lying nor
would I hold this against someone else *outside* the game... in fact, I'd
probably appreciate it! I *like* the Machiavellian aspect of this game.

As far as the Sucky Club goes, I would have no problem stealing the SC
player's vampires and not returning them in order to help me win. I also
wouldn't be offered this deal, no doubt, especially after this post :)

But this type of deal-breaking is only possible for the person that is
*offered* a deal and therefore it is likely that the deal will be offered to
people who are a) trustworthy b) fools c) friends.

It is (b) and (c) which should concern us. Without opening the collusion
can'o'worms again, I have to say that I have seen this type of thing happen
at a recent tournament and though I didn't end up complaining to the judge
(well... publicly), I was mighty miffed about it. This was further
complicated by the fact that one of the two players was obviously *not*
colluding, simply taking advatage of the other player's (his best friend)
lack of playiing skill (read: intellect). When someone offers you a win with
no distingusihable downside, you take it, right? If that doesn't benefit the
person who offered it, you don't care, right? Anyway...

I would hate to see interesting strategies disappear with the banning of the
Sucky Club, but I'd really rather not show up at tournaments where,
regardless of the quality of my deck and my skill at playing this game, the
players who take advantage of the SC win the game every time. I also don't
want to have to wait for 20 minutes while other players decide on the nature
of their deal. Ultimately, I'd like to play too.

While I realize there is no democracy to this decision, my vote is for
banning Sucky Club for competitive play if only to remove an obvious avenue
of collusion. Failing that, an acceptable alternative would be modifying the
card so that it is harder to abuse. And let me just state for the record
that I hate that this is becoming necessary. And while I can appreciate a
good back-stabbing in-game, I can't stand the fact that anyone who plays
this game would actively *cheat* in order to win tournaments. It's just a
fucking game.

Cheers,
WES

Here's an interesting theory. Contrary to current rulings and
interpretations, deal-breaking should be mandatory in most instances.
Let's say my prey is Potence CrushRush and I'm running a nasty
Tzimisce Fry'em. Rather than play our rightful places in the jyhad, a
table-split is the order of the day. I'll help my prey take 3 VP and
then s/he'll roll over and I get the final 2 VP. OK, arguably we are
making a deal that maximizes our VP expectation. Seating is an
in-game consideration, and beating each other up is uncertain, a game
of chance, a crapshoot, (a card game...) My prey starts working on
their prey, and I also start working on their prey, Eagle's Sighting
anywhere it's needed on the table to keep everyone else IN until "we"
can roll over them. My prey gobbles up 1-2-3 victory points. Does
s/he keep the Deal, roll over, and die regardless of relative
position-strength at this moment? Let's reassess the Deal at this
point. Dealkeeping pros: reputation (out-of-game, surely i'll never
go for this deal with this person again if the deal is broken.)
Dealkeeping cons: Failing to take 2 more (read maximizing) VP in the
current game (the rule-stated and mandated GOAL of the tournament
game.) When the deal was made it was allowable, but living up to the
deal may no longer be allowed by the rules. Oh, and another con: this
kind of dealmaking may become impossible in future games because of
this shift in deal-dynamics. (Or is that a pro? Anyway, this
consideration is also certainly out-of-game.) Vampires are and should
be a treacherous lot, and methuselahs should be among the most
treacherous.
Alternately, a card like this could be printed:
Smoochy-Smoochy
Master. This Methuselah is allowed to roll over and die to keep an
in-game deal, even if it costs them a VP or 2 in the current game.
or
Consanguinous Footsie-playing
Political action. Called at +1 stealth, worth 1 vote. Successful
referendum means this methuselah may name any terms for
tablesplitting, and later live up to these terms. If this Methuselah
also controls the succubus club, s/he may leave the table with a
chosen methuselah for up to 10 minutes of safe sex in a back room or
parked sport utility vehicle (only on their untap phase.)
-spinney the unharmonious

changing/banning, other rulings that facilitate its abuse should be
re-examined. Time abuse (most important problem, imho) should be
harder with or without it. Table-splitting as currently allowed is
also a big prob. Don't know what to do about instantaneous free
outlandish game imbalance; that might be an actual problem with the
card.

bow out of this debate now, before they look like a fool.) The Club
permits someone to turn a mid-cap deck into a weenie deck in one untap

TOO MUCH GAME SWING

Here is my biggest problem with the card. Deals have always existed but after
players agree to do something they still have to be able to pull it off. The
actions that are then taken toward fullfilling the deal are all subject to the
same foils as before the deal was made. However, deals made with the SC can be,
in the same instant, agreed to and completed. There are no cards to foil the
trade and the swing in the balance is HUGE. One of the things that got RTI
banned was the "instant death" aspect of the card. I believe Scott stated as
much somewhere. In any event we can see that the errata he issued addressed the
instant death aspect of the card by putting a sort of fuse on its instant death
effect. This gives players a chance to react. The swings that can be brought
about by SC deals are just as great and there is no fuse.

NOT A NEW PROBLEM

Our games were simply "not fun at all" about 4 years ago when SC was big in LA.
After repeated tournaments ending with unhappy people (and yes, the SC did win
tournaments!) a bunch of players made a pact not to deal with anyone who played
the SC--at all costs. I was offered a deal once in a game by a SC player. I
declined his offer. As punishment he gave all his minions (weenie horde) to my
predator who ousted me immediately. We did send emails to LSJ asking that the
card be banned. It was probably around the same time as our Madness of the Bard
suggestion. We have had trouble--this is not new. I know its a bit out of
character for the L.A. crowd to stop playing with a card that we all agreed was
very very powerful but we did anyway. It had enough of a negative effect on the
fun factor that we simply dropped it. Not until two of us slipped it into our
Los Angeles qualifier decks did the card reappear. We both qualified. And the
card had a big effect on many of the rounds we played in.

UNDERCOSTED

I'd also like to suggest that the card is tremendously undercosted. (originally
Tatu's argument). There are only 10 unique masters in the game that don't have
a clan requirement, a pool cost, or a built-in burn clause. I'm also going to
exclude Metro Underground since it has a pool cost when used. The first 4 of
these 10 can either be stolen of have their counters stolen as part of a
built-in weakener.

A. Location Stealable or Counters Stealable
High Museum of Art, Atlanta (may be stolen)
Powerbase: Montreal (stealable)
Rack, The (may steal rack)
Powerbase: Rome (may steal counters)

If nothing else, the sheer utility of the Succubus Club should keep if from
being lumped together with the other 5 cards in this group.

Elysium: The Arboretum (ends some combats)
Information Highway (speed of xfers)
Police Department (press)
Barrens, The (cycle)
Storage Annex (store a useful card)
Succubus Club (see the cards in a willing partner's hand, give pool to any
player you want to, get pool from any player willing to give it, give negative
controlled cards away during your untap to avoid their effects (Milicent Smith,
Charnas, Famed or Society of Leopold vamp) and others), cycle your hand via a
Capuchin Visit, give your minions to a willing partner to help them overwhelm
someone, give useful cards from hand to someone who needs 'em, get cards from
someone's hand willing to help you, share useful controlled cards with a willing
partner (both use The Rack, Army of Rats, gain extra life on your regenrating
allies,double the rate of Temptation counter accumulation, increase or decrease
the Smiling Jack counter accumulation, )...

I'd love to see the card hamstrung in the Camarilla reprint. Make it
non-tradeable and reduce the number of trades that can be made. Maybe even make
it burnable or temporary.

another dedicated combat deck by their own logic.

Playing pure combat with no combat defense and sitting as a rush deck's

legislate, since you can make lots of transfers and just happen to tap out

Honour is like the hawk: sometimes it must go hooded.

I don't consider breaking a deal to be any indication of someone's honour as
a player; cheating however is a big thing with me. I will not play with
anyone who cheats and I would never even *consider* cheating in a game. It
just wouldn't cross my mind. I want to win this game based on skill and not
have to rely on subterfuge.

However, deals are a totally different animal. Honestly, part of me wishes
deals in this game did not exist at all, as they often seem to result in two
players taking the fun away from three players, at least some of the time.
But they do exist, and the Predator-Prey dynamics facilitate them to some
degree, with or without Sucky Club et al. There is an implicit 'deal' with
anyone who sits across the table from you... you have no reason to harm them
and they have no reason to harm you (in theory; in practice Detroit games
are nothing like this :).

I can count on half of one hand the number of times that I have actually
broken a deal.

I can however say that in every deal I have made, I have considered breaking
that particular deal *every* time I take my turn. I always have to consider
whether a deal is worth keeping (or making) based on my chances to win the
game.

I will always make a deal with my predator because I prefer fighting on one
front to two. By contrast, I will (almost) never make a deal with my prey.
They're just a sack of pool and a VP on my way to victory. And in Linc's
case, I guess they're also a ride home... an out-of-game consideration,
albeit an important one :)

Although it is frustrating to have a deal broken on you (and I have had far
more deals broken on me than *I* have broken), it is also usually pretty
funny. I don't hold grudges for this. Any player that is not putting his or
her self-interest before all other considerations is not playing at the top
of their level. Selfishness is a virtue in this game, like it or not.

I remember when we tried to get my friend Jason to play Jyhad back when it
came out. Jason is highly intelligent, a fantastic chess player but *not* a
'gamer'. In this game, he had a strong position, though was still having
trouble understanding the concepts. Everyone was trying to make deals with
him, especially me (I was his prey). In the end, he made a deal with me and
others and then promptly broke them all as soon as I was tapped and he could
bleed me out. 'Fuck it! I can't keep track of any of these deals, so back to
basics. Bleed. Bleed. Bleed'. I was ousted, but more importantly I was
laughing my ass off. It still amuses me. It's just too bad he didn't keep up
the game. We need people like him.

> I know we've had LOTS of funny moments[1] where someone was about to
> take a deal, and then thought about it and asked a clarification and gets
a
> "Well, I didn't say THAT..." I really find that to be half the fun of

It's cheesy, but it's oh so funny. I've fallen victim to this so often that
I'd probably take the time to write out a contract stating all the terms if
given the chance :) Of course, no contract would be binding and I'd be the
first one to add loopholes. It's not my fault you didn't read the fine
print!

> [1] A personal favorite of mine was David Tatu telling his prey "If you
> don't vote that down, I'm going to bleed you!" which got it voted down.
He
> promptly bled her next turn, of course.

This kind of thing can be overdone. A player in the last Toronto tournament
kept trying to make deals when he had nothing to offer aside from *not*
rushing with his Assamites. It was pretty silly. If you bleed me I will rush
you. If you assign a KRC point to me I will rush you. If you don't give me
some of that Parity Shift, I'll rush you. THOSE are fair enough... but when
he started to threaten *every* player on *every* action they made, it was
retarded. If you (player across the table) are deflected and bleed me, I
will rush you. If you (player across the table) don't play a 5th to fill my
guys I will rush you. After a while, nobody gave a shit and just ignored him
speaking as a serious waste of the allotted two hours.

Some deals really don't need to be made. And sometimes, you just have to
accept that your predator is going to try to oust you. It's their job.

Cheers,
WES

Let's apply the argument. I'll take a card that was printed, then
banned with a variant being printed that has since been errated:
Stake/Wooden Stake.

In the core set, we have the Stake:
Stake: Melee Weapon. Inflicts strenth damage as a strike. If Stake
does more than one damage in combat, opposive vampire is paralyzed.
If opposing vampire is paralyzed, they gain control of the stake.

Well, when we changed names, we also took rules for paralysis from the
game, and the card got banned, and reprinted as the Wooden Stake.

Wooden Stake: Melee Weapon. Inflicts strength damage as a strike. If
two or more damage is done with the Wooden Stake in combat, the damage
is treated as aggravated. If opposing vampire goes to torpor, they
gain control of the Wooden Stake and do not untap while in torpor.

Well, this implied that the Wooden Stake could burn vampires, so they
found it necessary to errata the card. Now, if we follow the argument
that it's better to ban the card and reprint the variant, we would see
the Wooden Stake banned, and a new card printed:

Sharp, Pointy Stick: Melee Weapon....(we all know what the Wooden
Stake does now I hope, so i'll stop regurgitating card text).

What happens if that new text is deemed unbalancing? A fourth card?

How many useless cards do you want your collection to have? Fifteen
variants of the same card, all of which are banned because, with each
variant, someone found a way to screw the metagame with it?

While it's frustrating to new players to pick up a copy of, say,
Jyahd-Fame, and then find out the card does something else entirely --
it's more frustrating to have a significant portion of your card stock
banned, only to have the next set make you start over with a card with
nearly identical functionality. Under the current system, old cards
are still playable, provided you've done a little bit of homework in
advance. Under the other system, the cards are flat-out unplayable no
matter how much homework you do.

The Fanboy

When the deal is made, you have to establish whether it's in the
player's interests when the deal is made.

With a re-write to something along the lines of "You must backstab", you
have to establish at (virtually) *every* *single* *point* in the game

same problems as now increased by an arbitrary amount (I hesitate to say
an order of magnitude, though it feels not dis-similar).

>fun to play out; 2 players beating up on one is a near-foregone conclusion,
>and is the WHOLE GODDAMN REASON for having the predator-prey relationship:

Not entirely (though, of course, this is an important facet of the
relationship). For instance, a political deck very specifically has far
more leeway in this respect, clearly not an accident.

The predator-prey relationship attempts to make it harder, with the Edge
and pool for ousting being a carrot, to turn the entire game into a game
of diplomacy and negotiation - each player has separate interests and
separate abilities.

I would be interested in any ways, with cards and the mechanisms they
provide, that the ganging up/table splitting deals could be discouraged.
Cards which mess around with the fringes of ousting and victory
conditions - like Political Flux and Lextalionis - strike me as a
potential option.
